weathering._why_exterior: VP8-EXT (2026-09-02). The 400m approach stand (`hall_approach`, `hall_gate`) judged the works still 'the clean cream castle kit with pale towers' -- the shader was already reaching every kit tower/roof surface (`stronghold.gd::_weather_hall_massing`) and every outer curtain wall, coping, merlon, buttress, gate jamb/arch and skirt facing (all already textured through `_stone_shader_material`), but every one of those surfaces was sharing the SAME weathering intensity as the five lit rooms inside, and the kit's own retinted LightRock/DarkRock tint (building_prefabs.json, ~#817f78/#68675f) is a mid-value grey-tan on its own -- no amount of joint moss over that base reads as 'dark ruined mass' at range. This block is read ONLY by `stronghold.gd::_material`/`_stone_shader_material` callers that pass `exterior: true` (every genuinely outside-facing stone: kit massing, outer walls, coping/merlons/buttresses, the gate frame and arch, the skirt foundation) and OVERRIDES the block above term-by-term; the five interior chambers (`outer: false` walls, the floor, the ceiling) never read this block and are unchanged. `darken`/`desaturate` bias the TINT itself before the shader's own texture and moss terms are added, which is the lever the flat parity pass upstream (building_prefabs.json's own T1-HALL-4 value-drop notes) could not reach because it only ever retints the kit's raw StandardMaterial3D before this shader replaces it. `damp_height` is 2.2x the interior figure because the 'lower third' the approach silhouette needs covered is a fraction of a 15-38m tower, not a 6-22m chamber wall -- the interior number was measured against the room the player stands in, this one against the mass the player walks toward.
weathering._why_exterior_round2: VP-HALL-FIX (2026-09-02), a code-blind judge re-reading fresh 100/200/400m frames after the round-1 block above landed: 'still pale cream towers and curtain walls with no weathering, no moss, no dark mass'. A headless material dump (`tools/_diag_hall_materials.gd`) confirmed every exterior surface WAS already textured through this shader with `exterior:true` -- the routing was never the bug. The bug is that `darken: 0.24` against the kit's #817f78/#68675f retint only reaches a shader `tint` of about (0.38,0.38,0.36), which is BRIGHTER than `site.stone_light` (#66655e, ~0.40 direct but close enough to read as the SAME value) -- the 'weathered ruin' tint was landing almost exactly on top of the ordinary LIT-INTERIOR wall tone instead of below it, so no amount of moss on top of it could read as a dark mass against the sky. `darken` 0.24 -> 0.56 and `desaturate` 0.32 -> 0.5 pushes the same #817f78 kit tint down to roughly (0.21,0.21,0.20) -- clearly darker than the interior stone_light and darker than the current stone_skirt tier (#575147, ~0.31), which is what 'dark ruined mass against the sky' actually requires. Moss/damp are lifted too: JUDGE-6/T1-HALL wanted moss and damp to be VISIBLE, not merely present in a shader param nobody could see over a base that was too pale to show it.
weathering._why_exterior_round3: VP-HALL-FIX-3 (2026-09-02), owner evidence at 400m/200m: the Hall still does not separate from the ground -- low contrast against the sky persists even with round 2's darker tint. `darken` 0.56 -> 0.74 (desaturate left at 0.5) pushes the same #817f78 kit tint down to roughly (0.13,0.13,0.12), a further ~40% relative cut in the SAME proportion round 1->round 2 already took ((1-0.74)/(1-0.56) = 0.59, close to round 2's own 0.58 factor over round 1), so the ladder this block's own `_comment_piece_variation` describes (skirt < works walls < DarkRock < LightRock) holds exactly as before -- `darken`/`desaturate` multiply every exterior stone's tint uniformly before moss/damp are added, so a proportional push cannot invert which tier is darkest, it only deepens all of them together. This is a silhouette-only lever: interior chambers never read this block (see `_why_exterior` above) and are unchanged.
weathering._why_exterior_round5: DECISION-hall-sentries.md FAILURE A (2026-09-02). `darken` 0.48 -> 0.0. `Color.darkened` multiplies in sRGB, so 0.48 was ×0.24 in linear light, applied on top of `T_UnevenBrick_BaseColor` whose own mean is 0.202 linear -- effective albedo 0.011, below coal (0.04), which no lighting change can rescue. Any darken value above ~0.15 puts the whole facade under the ACES toe. `desaturate` and the moss/damp/streak values below are unchanged.
weathering._why_exterior_round4: VP-HALL-FIX ITEM1 (2026-09-02). A code-blind judge at the GATE stand (100m and the gate itself, not the 200/400m stands round 3 was tuned against): 'a flat black cutout up close AND at the gate'. Round 3's `darken` 0.74, stacked with `hall_stone.gdshader`'s own distance-darken curve and `fog_disabled`, over-darkened the near read that round 3 never measured. `Color.darkened(x)` multiplies each RGB channel by `(1-x)` and does not touch luminance ORDER, only magnitude, so the required check is arithmetic, not a render: the kit's LightRock retint #817f78 (r0.5059,g0.498,b0.4706) has luminance (Godot's 0.2125/0.7154/0.0721 weights) 0.4977; at `darken` 0.74 the tint's own luminance is 0.26*0.4977=0.1294, i.e. 33/255 -- comfortably under the dispatch's 60/255 floor and the arithmetic reason the gate stand crushed to black BEFORE the distance curve or any lighting even applies. `darken` 0.74 -> 0.48 (desaturate held at 0.5 -- desaturate lerps toward the tint's OWN luminance, so it cannot move the luminance number itself) puts tint luminance at 0.52*0.4977=0.2588, i.e. 66/255: above the 60 floor with a working margin, still well under round 1's 0.24 (luminance 96/255, the 'clean cream castle' complaint) and under round 2's 0.56 (56/255, itself already short of 60). THE LADDER (skirt < works walls < DarkRock < LightRock) holds exactly as round 3's own note says it must: this is the SAME multiplier applied to every exterior-tagged tint, so a proportional change cannot reorder tiers, only rescale all of them together -- works walls' own base (#66655e, luminance 0.3949) lands at 0.52*0.3949=0.2054 (52/255), still below LightRock's 66/255 as the ladder requires. THE 400m SILHOUETTE TRADE: `hall_stone.gdshader`'s own `distance_darken_floor` ALSO moved (0.7 -> 0.85, required independently by the same dispatch item -- see that uniform's own comment) which by itself would LOSE far-range darkening, but the base tint drop more than covers it in absolute terms while the sky the silhouette is judged against is brighter still (an unlit, largely diffuse-shaded stone versus open sky ambient), so the darker-than-sky contrast this whole system exists to protect is not spent by either change alone.

_comment_approach_pylons: BAND5-CONTENT, prompt 66. Three of that prompt's asks are one object, so they are built once rather than three times: the `navigation spine` ("pylons/landmarks should create readable world-space direction without becoming magical GPS"), `pylon/tether machinery readability`, and the environmental storytelling clause ("use existing machinery ... rather than inventing unrelated lore"). Band 5 had NONE of it. The chapter's conduit network stopped at the relay (z 3749) and the quarry (z 1790) and the last 680m -- the approach to the thing the whole network feeds -- was open meadow with a castle on the horizon. The run is the answer: an unbroken, LIT trunk line arriving at the works, the exact opposite statement to the seven spokes' broken-and-dead runs, and the same one `old_quarry.json`'s own `_comment_pylons` already makes (D41: present-tense machinery doing present-tense harm, not ruins).
_comment_approach_pylons_why_a_line: Why a straight line beside a wandering road, and not pylons ON the road. The trail's own Band 5 waypoints swing +-80m either side of x=0 (terrain_playground.json `trail.bands`), which is what stops the region being a corridor. A line that followed it would be a handrail -- literally magical GPS in world geometry, the thing the prompt names. A STRAIGHT line the road keeps crossing is the opposite: it is a BEARING. The player loses sight of it around every rise, meets it again, and each time it is pointing the same way. Direction comes from the line's own convergence in perspective, which is free and needs no marker, no minimap and no objective arrow.
_comment_approach_pylons_measured: SITED BY MEASUREMENT, not by guess -- `tools/_probe_band5_pylon_line.gd`, which exists to answer the one question a config cannot: `severed_spokes.gd::_conduit_span` sags the cable `distance * 0.05` below an attachment at `height * 0.66` computed from EACH pylon's OWN base, so ground rising between two stations pushes itself up into a cable derived from the two ends. The first candidate (13 stations, 9m) put the cable 1.74m over the ground on span 4->5 -- head height on a 1.8m player, a defect that shows only in a render. The probe swept height against station count: 15 stations at 10.0m is the SMALLEST height that clears comfortably, worst clearance 3.14m. Relief across the run is 11.77m (-3.46 to 8.31), which is why this had to be measured at all. Re-run the probe before moving any station.
_comment_approach_pylons_healing: This run needs no ending work and gets its payoff for free. `meadow_healing.json`'s `tether_lights` finds every LIT Team Tether fitting by WHAT ITS MATERIAL IS rather than by node name, precisely so the three files that build pylons all pay off together -- so all fifteen of these go dark on the walk home from the Warden, along with the quarry's four and the relay's. The last region to get the network is also the last to lose it, in the player's own line of sight.

approach_pylons._comment_round2:
Blind visual pass round 1 called the pylons "the best thing in the survey" and the wire between them "a bezier debug line, not a hanging cable -- cables sag, they do not soar", concluding "the wire connecting them undoes them." So the fix is the wire. `severed_spokes.gd::_conduit_span` sags a span by `distance * 0.05 * sag_scale`, and sag is PROPORTIONAL TO SPAN -- the default 1.0 was tuned on the spokes' and the quarry's ~14m spans, where it droops 0.7m and reads; over this run's 35m spans it droops 1.8m over five times the length, which is a straight diagonal. 2.2 takes it to 11% of span.

Sag and ground clearance pull directly against each other, so both were swept together rather than either being guessed (`tools/_sweep_cable.gd`): at the old 10.0m height, 2.2 puts the cable 1.01m off the ground -- under a walking player. 12.0m is the height that buys the sag back, and it is the SMALLEST of the swept heights that keeps a 2.2x sag clear of 2.2m (worst 2.33m). The cost is a pylon 20% taller than the one the critic liked, which is the trade taken deliberately: a decisive fix that round 2 can actually see, over a timid one that changes nothing.
approach_pylons._comment_height: ROUND 2: 10.0 -> 12.0, see `_comment_round2` -- the height is now set by the CABLE, not by the pylon. Original reasoning, still true: against the quarry spur run's 4.6m. This is the trunk that feeds the Hall and it should out-scale every spur the player has met; 10.0 is also the measured floor for cable clearance (see `_comment_approach_pylons_measured`) rather than a number picked for drama. `_build_pylons` scales the one GLB uniformly, so a 10m pylon is a 4.6m pylon at 2.17x -- heavier as well as taller, which is the correct read for a trunk.

_comment_approach_drain: BAND5-CONTENT, prompt 66's environmental storytelling clause. The full reasoning, and an honest statement of the half of the effect this does NOT own, is in `scripts/world/approach_drain_skin.gd`'s header. The short version: `terrain_playground.json`'s `drains.stations` holds seven entries, four at the quarry (z~1790) and three at the relay (z~3749), and NONE in Band 5 -- so the drained ground got weaker the closer the player walked to the machine draining it. `bounds` is the corridor the fifteen `approach_pylons` run through, with margin; the skin's alpha is `playground_heightfield.drain_factor()` itself, so it paints exactly where a station says and NOTHING anywhere else. It therefore renders nothing today and says so in the build log: `drains.stations` is a file no Gate D lane may edit (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT §5), so the Band 5 stations are REQUESTED in this lane's report the same way a `density_scale` is, and this is shipped ahead of them so that granting the request is one edit to one data file rather than an edit plus a code change.

Wraps the pylon run (x -40 -> -8 over z 7010 -> 7505) with roughly 22m of margin west and east, which carries the widest station radius the request asks for without sampling ground the drain can never reach. Cell 4.0 against the relay skin's 3.0 because this corridor is 540m long rather than 92m across and the alpha gradient here is broad -- a finer cell would multiply quads to no visible end. _comment_language: R8.2's brief: a sacred natural site INDUSTRIALISED by Tether. The same grammar `SE23` uses at the relay, at full scale here. _comment_interior_structure: CONTENT-0828B. Owner playtest 2026-08-28 sec4a: 'burrow warrens and the castle are the lame looking locations. basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building.' He named a CLASS of space rather than two sites, so the answer is a shared method -- scripts/world/interior_structure.gd, which burrow_warrens.json consumes from the same file with a different vocabulary. That file's header carries the mechanism; the short version is that a chamber assembled from six flat boxes has exactly two scales of incident (the room, and its props) where the meadow outside has five or six, and the missing MIDDLE scale is why an interior reads as blockout however good its texture is. The five passes supply it: a vertical member at a repeating pitch along every wall (`bays`), a jointed band at mid-height (`course`), ceiling ribs landed on the same divisions so wall and roof read as one structure (`ribs`), a jamb-and-lintel frame around every cut opening (`reveals`), and a post in each internal corner (`corners`). None of it is solid, none of it enters a doorway, and none of it reaches further into a room than interior_structure.gd's MAX_PROJECT_M -- half the metre `combat_arena_bounds_at()` reserves from every wall, so the Warden fight keeps the arena it was tuned against. `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off. _comment_interior_structure_castle: This building's VOCABULARY, against the cave's. `jitter: 0` is the difference in code: masonry lands on its pitch exactly, and any lean at all reads as a mistake rather than as rock. `bay_pitch_m` 3.6 against the cave's 2.9 -- these spaces are 16-28m across and up to 22m tall, and the cave's tighter pitch would crowd a hall. This does NOT replace `trim` above: those are Team Tether girders and conduit, faction hardware bolted onto the stone, and they say who occupies the building; this is the building. Roles take the castle's own three stone values via stronghold.gd::_structure_colour (`stone` for shafts and corners, `stone_light` for capitals and the course, `stone_dark` for ribs and reveals) so nothing here introduces a fourth stone -- add a `tints` block here to override any role. The value steps matter more than they look: every interior light in this complex sets shadow_enabled=false, so a member proud of a wall is lit almost exactly like the wall behind it and only the value separates them.

hall_occupation._comment_brazier_reach_t1_hall_4: T1-HALL-4, 2026-08-30, JUDGE-6 defect 12, and read this BEFORE adding a light -- the lane very nearly did and it would have been wrong. The judge's words are "the four braziers are lit, but the towers immediately behind them are uniformly dark with NO FALLOFF POOL AT ALL. The flames are unlit sprites", and `torch_prop.gd`'s own header says it carries no light and that callers add their own -- which together read exactly like a missing OmniLight3D. They are not missing. `stronghold.gd::_build_hall_fire` has always given every entry in this list a real flickering light at the `energy` and `range` written here. What is wrong is the REACH and the SHAPE. The four causeway bowls sit at z -24 and -40; the gate towers they stand in front of rise from the plinth at z about -13, so their bodies are 10-30m from the nearest flame and a 15m range simply stops short of them. Range 15 -> 26 on those four only (the two yard fires are lighting a yard, and reach nothing by design). `energy` is deliberately NOT raised: the deck immediately around each bowl is already correctly exposed, and more energy would blow that out to fix something 20m away. `attenuation` 1.6 is the shape half. Godot's default 1.0 falls off almost linearly to the range edge, spreading a fire's contribution thinly over everything rather than pooling it; above 1.0 concentrates it near the source. A longer range at the default attenuation would have made the whole approach slightly warmer and still produced no pool, which is the defect. NO NEW LIGHTS. `_comment_braziers` above spends the section 7 budget down to its ceiling of 18 exactly, and `_report_light_budget` counts these six; a seventh omni here would breach a budget the design states in a number.
